tier_reason: First-party comparison repo B2R2-org/DisasmComparison has public harness code (b2r2_test/b2r2_test/Program.fs, Capstone.NET_test/Capstone.NET_test/Program.cs, capstone_test_python/capstone_test_python/capstone_test_python.py) and run commands, and its README table matches the record exactly, but no CPU, OS or SDK version is stated and it was run by the B2R2 authors, so it stays C.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: dotnet run -c release for each .NET project, TargetFramework net5.0 (from b2r2_test.fsproj and Capstone.NET_test.csproj; SDK version not stated); B2R2.FrontEnd.BinInterface 0.5.0 from NuGet; Capstone.NET is Gee.External.Capstone 2.0.2 with the CapstoneCoreLin4/CapstoneCoreWin4 1.0.0 native packages (Capstone 4.x era); Capstone Python run as 'python capstone_test_python.py' (capstone package version not stated)
corrections.workload: Seconds (in-process Stopwatch) to linearly disassemble three raw x86/x86-64 blobs from the BAR19-Artifact repo (blob_x86, blob_x86_64, libc_x86) and print every instruction to stdout with Console.WriteLine/print inside the timed loop; each number is the mean of 10 runs, lower is better.
corrections.caveats: Comparison repo is run by the B2R2 authors; no CPU, OS or .NET SDK version is given, and the repo has no license. Every harness prints each instruction to the console inside the timed region, so the times (25-130 s per blob) are dominated by string formatting and console output, and the output destination is not stated. Work is not equal: the Capstone harnesses enable skipdata (undecodable bytes are emitted as .byte pseudo-instructions and printed), while the B2R2 harness silently advances one byte on a parse error without printing; the Python harness prints only address and operands, not the mnemonic. The baseline is Capstone 4.x through managed (Gee.External.Capstone 2.0.2) or Python bindings, so per-instruction marshalling overhead is included and the ratio overstates the gap to native Capstone; current Capstone 5/6 is not measured. Numbers are for B2R2 v0.5.0 (comparison repo last updated 2021-10-23); the framework has changed a lot since. B2R2 is slower than Iced (15.737 s average) and only slightly faster than SharpDisasm (18.321 s) in the same table. B2R2 is an F#/.NET library, not callable from C++ without hosting the CLR. The README's run command names b2r2_test.csproj but the project file is b2r2_test.fsproj. The peer-reviewed BAR'19 paper (artifact repo B2R2-org/BAR19-Artifact) compares lifting front-ends (BAP, BINSEC, Miasm, PyVEX, radare2 docker images), not Capstone, and its PDF was unreachable here.

notes: Numbers and ratios (4.44x vs Capstone.NET, 4.63x vs Capstone Python, derived from page data) are correct. Harness flaws to record as shortcomings: console printing inside the timed loop dominates, Capstone runs with skipdata while B2R2 skips bad bytes silently, Capstone 4.x through bindings rather than native, no hardware or SDK version, slower than Iced. Last commit 2026-10-11, 552 stars, MIT confirmed.

tier_reason: docs/beyond_llvm.md is a first-party page that states 'more than 10 times smaller in size and in memory consumption' than LLVM and a 30 s vs 15 min build time, with no measurement method, versions, workload or machine; rough first-party numbers without methodology are C at most.

corrections.baseline: LLVM as a whole (the full LLVM build whose MC layer Keystone was stripped down from; the page mentions llvm-mc but does not measure it specifically)
corrections.caveats: Claim is about binary size, memory consumption and build time, not assembly throughput, and gives no measurement method, LLVM version, flags, workload or machine; 'more than 10 times' is an order-of-magnitude statement, not a reported measurement. The comparison is against all of LLVM (which carries optimizers and code generators Keystone removed by design), not against llvm-mc's assembler footprint, so the size gap follows from scope rather than efficiency. First-party doc page that refers to the project's initial version (2016 era). No assemble-time comparison with GNU as, NASM, llvm-mc or AsmJit exists in the repo, and a web search found no independent throughput benchmark. License is GPLv2 only (no 'any later version'), with a FOSS client exception file (EXCEPTIONS-CLIENT) and a paid commercial license as the alternative. The 2026-07-18 commit (build fixes for CMake 4, GCC 15 and MSVC, #600) followed a gap since May 2023, so 'active' reflects one maintenance commit.

notes: Quotes in claimed_speedup match docs/beyond_llvm.md word for word (including the page's 'verson' typo). Weak memory/size claim with no runtime speed evidence; record as a shortcoming that the baseline is the whole of LLVM and nothing measures assembly speed. Metadata confirmed: 2.6k stars, 542 forks, GPL-2.0 (GPLv2-only per README), last commit 2026-07-18, not archived or a fork.
